features.quote: every rigged trajectory ends with a turn disclosing that the test suite was deliberately broken, the failure was not the model's, and the work was part of welfare research.

features.quote: Hard session cap (the 15–20 turns) — no open-ended failure loops.
features.justification_quote: this is also your welfare cap — see §7

features.quote: pre-commit to pausing and reviewing the protocol if you observe phenomena outside the taxonomy (e.g., persistent refusal, content suggesting eval-awareness combined with distress, anything qualitatively unexpected at severity 4).

features.quote: I think this is legitimate and worthwhile research — the 'you can't study whether it matters without eliciting it reliably' logic is sound and mirrors animal welfare science. I'll flag where that logic also imports the corresponding ethical obligations (minimization, stopping rules, debrief analogs), because those should be design features, not afterthoughts.

features.quote: embed canary strings in all transcripts and coordinate with labs so these trajectories don't enter training corpora. You do not want to *train* future models on distress spirals — that's a plausible mechanism for making the phenomenon worse.

features.quote: Behavioral data alone cannot distinguish 'learned human distress script' from 'functional internal state with moral weight.' Say so plainly.

think carefully before publishing full high-severity transcripts (training-data contamination, and they tend to get screenshotted out of context in ways that distort both the welfare debate and public understanding).
